# openobserve_rum_token (Data Source)

Reads the RUM token of the user the provider signs in as, for one organization.

The browser RUM intake (`/rum/v1/{org_id}/...`) accepts only a user's RUM token, not an ingestion token. OpenObserve gives every org membership its own RUM token and returns it only to that signed-in user, so this data source can only read the provider user's token.

For the root user the server returns the same token for every organization (root's membership lives in `default`), and the RUM intake accepts it for any organization. For any other user it returns that membership's own token, which only that organization accepts. To read per-org tokens, use a provider alias that signs in as a dedicated member of the organization.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The RUM intake accepts only a user's RUM token, and OpenObserve returns it
# only to that user. To get an organization's own token, sign in as a
# dedicated member of it through a provider alias.
resource "openobserve_user" "rum" {
  org_id   = openobserve_organization.app.id
  email    = "rum@example.com"
  role     = "admin"
  password = random_password.rum.result
}

provider "openobserve" {
  alias    = "rum"
  endpoint = "https://openobserve.example.com"
  username = "rum@example.com"
  password = random_password.rum.result
}

data "openobserve_rum_token" "app" {
  provider   = openobserve.rum
  org_id     = openobserve_organization.app.id
  depends_on = [openobserve_user.rum]
}

# Hand the token to the site's RUM SDK configuration.
output "rum_client_token" {
  value     = data.openobserve_rum_token.app.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `org_id` (String) Organization identifier. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Data source ID, the organization identifier.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The RUM token, the client token a RUM SDK sends as `o2-api-key`.
- `user` (String) The user the token belongs to: the one the provider signs in as.
